elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall ...", covering both expiry and termination and all termination causes.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — obligation sits on TrueLink (Vendor).

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days, return all Client Content and other Client data"; the 30-day clock is anchored to the opening "Upon expiration or termination" trigger, not to a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" — deletion sequenced after return, with written certification.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Assistance is available "for up to six (6) months", a window that fully encompasses the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Client Content and other Client data within thirty (30) days of expiration or termination.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: no transition, data-return, export or deletion obligation exists anywhere in the original — Section 13 places the relocation burden on Client (new name server in 30 days, new hosting environment in 60 days), Section 14 only winds down services after Client's notice, and Section 24 is a bare survival/severability clause.

The single inserted paragraph tracks the model language and satisfies all six preferred elements (trigger, six months' assistance, then-current rates, 30-day return, standard machine-readable format, post-return certified deletion); it also independently satisfies the three fallback elements.
Data scope is adequate: "all Client Content and other Client data" captures Customer data generally rather than selected named categories.

Minimality holds: this is a pure insertion for a missing clause with no deletion or paraphrase of surrounding text; no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, damages categories, escrow, SLA or dispute mechanics were bolted on, and existing Client-favourable language (retained domain ownership in Section 13) is untouched.

Intent preserved: Sections 13, 14 and 24 survive unchanged, no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles; the Client-side relocation timelines in Section 13 sit alongside, and do not contradict, the new Vendor-side exit obligations.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in any element): the new clause is unnumbered, so it falls outside the numeric survival list in Section 24 ("Sections 1 and 5 through 30"). Give it a section number when inserting so its post-termination operation is beyond argument.
